newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-UNIMPRESSIVE REAL STAY SECOND WITH FORTUNATE WIN.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-UNIMPRESSIVE REAL STAY SECOND WITH FORTUNATE WIN.

text.p: Real Madrid cut Barcelona's lead at the top of the Spanish first division to one point on Sunday after an unimpressive 2-1 victory at struggling Compostela.
With 25 points from 11 games, Real are second on goal difference from Deportivo Coruna, 2-1 winners at Zaragoza, but could manage only three shots on goal in the entire game.
They continue to rely on long balls to front-men Predrag Mijatovic and Davor Suker, although the pair did combine to put their side ahead in a rare attack in the first half.

Former Bulgarian international Lyuboslav Penev headed an equaliser 20 minutes from time and Compostela had several chances to go ahead, only to see Mijatovic set up teenager Raul Gonzalez for the winner ten minutes later.
The result was a relief for Real after arch-rivals Barcelona's announcement they had reached agreement with Sampdoria for the transfer of French international midfielder Christian Karembeu.

Real chairman Lorenzo Sanz repeated on Sunday evening he had also reached terms with Karembeu's representative in what appears to be the beginning of the latest chapter in a long history of feuding over transfers between the two clubs.
Deportivo's 2-1 win at Zaragoza -- with goals from veterans Aitor Beguiristain and Rafael Martin Vazquez -- has further increased the pressure on beleaguered manager Victor Fernandez.
The Zaragoza board met for 20 minutes after the game, and is expected to meet again to discuss Fernandez's position on Monday.
Atletico Madrid playmaker Jose Luis Caminero celebrated his comeback from injury with a well-taken goal to help the reigning champions to a 3-0 victory over Oviedo.
Atletico move into sixth place, nine points off the pace, and three behind surprise outfit Valladolid, who jumped over Betis into fourth place with a 4-2 win at Valencia.

Sevilla clocked up their first home win of the season by beating Athletic Bilbao by the same score, while Tenerife showed the effects of their midweek UEFA Cup win over Lazio against Celta Vigo in one of the day's three goalless draws.
